## Red check read (area o3-H) · 2026-11-17T19:41Z

`Test UI (2/16)` on head `5d3cef01` (job 134305171799) is a real red from this PR: `ui/packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts > generated Tailwind 4 pipeline > declares every theme token the component library declares` expected 39 tokens and got 34. The component library now declares `--color-chart-6..10`, and the CLI's generated app stylesheet does not yet. The seat folded that generator gap into this PR (claim amendment 6958535269 on #34902), and the fold round now running makes `app-generator.ts` emit `--chart-1..10` in light and dark. That clears this test. No re-run is requested.

<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02a290fe14b40d957ff586539d8f7521cb1b33af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b8f44efb6b43e168678b2ce56467d6f9f3f76342` — the merge of head `856cb45cb1da32a58e4ddc0e4602ceb8d5045c69` into base `02a290fe14b40d957ff586539d8f7521cb1b33af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b8f44efb6b43e168678b2ce56467d6f9f3f76342 && git checkout b8f44efb6b43e168678b2ce56467d6f9f3f76342
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 02a290fe14b40d957ff586539d8f7521cb1b33af 856cb45cb1da32a58e4ddc0e4602ceb8d5045c69 && git checkout -B drift-repro 02a290fe14b40d957ff586539d8f7521cb1b33af && git merge --no-ff 856cb45cb1da32a58e4ddc0e4602ceb8d5045c69

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02a290fe14b40d957ff586539d8f7521cb1b33af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T21:05Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `856cb45cb1da32a58e4ddc0e4602ceb8d5045c69`

Read against claim 6956247467, area amendment 6958512142 and seat amendment 6958535269 on #34902.
- **Size:** 13 files, +236/-16.
- **Not governed:** 0 of 13 paths on the register, 252 lines.
- **Merge-only head:** `856cb45c` is a merge of `main` onto `8047d355`. Comparing the `^[-+]` lines of the two diffs against their merge bases, they are byte-identical, so the code read below holds for both heads.
- **CI at this head:** still running (6 success, 10 skipped, 19 in progress, 0 failed). At `8047d355` it was 59 success, 12 skipped, with Test UI 16/16 after its re-run.
- **Claim surface:** all 13 files are inside it. The two shared harness tests and the catalog census re-pin are in 6958512142, and the cli and lint halves and their pins are in 6958535269.

This is **evidence only**. Once the live reading below is posted, this head is ACCEPT, with no push needed.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** `Fixes #34902` is right. The fallback palette is now ten theme tokens, so a 6- to 10-slice pie or donut no longer takes `palette[i % 5]`.
- **Tokens.**
  - `--chart-6..10` are defined in light and dark in both `@object-ui/components` and the Console stylesheet, each with its `--color-chart-N` alias.
  - The three fallback lists (`AdvancedChartImpl` `THEME_CHART_PALETTE`, and `CHART_COLORS` in `DashboardRenderer` and `DashboardGridLayout`) read all ten, with "kept in step" comments both ways.
  - An authored `colors` still wins, and a CONTROL pins it.
- **The fold.** The cli app generator emits `--chart-1..10` and the aliases in both themes, equal to the library's values, and a test compares them. This fixes the round-1 red token-parity pin. The `responsiveStyles` lint accepts `chart-6..10`, and `chart-11` still raises `style-unknown-token`.
- **Distinctness, measured.** CIEDE2000 from each new colour to its nearest neighbour is 15.2 to 27.7 across the four blocks. The existing palette's own worst pair is 13.1 to 22.6, so no new entry is closer than the palette already was.
- **Ablations.**
  - The three palettes each go red alone when their `--chart-6..10` entries are removed.
  - In the fold: the generator light tokens give 1 red, the aliases 2 red, and the lint 5 red.
  - Every restore was checked by blob.
- **Census re-pin.** `ChartRenderer.catalogRender-6939` moves by +10 gradients, +20 stops and +30 elements per fixture, with the text hash unchanged. That is the mechanical consequence of a longer palette.
- **Changeset.** It is a patch on six packages, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is right: no schema, and the authored `colors` is untouched.

### Must-fix
- **M1 (evidence): no live reading.** The card's done-when is "a 6- to 10-slice pie or donut draws every slice in a distinct colour **in light and dark themes**". The body says "I did not check the change in a real browser". The tests assert the `hsl(var(--chart-N))` strings Recharts is handed, not the colours the page paints. The house bar is that a UI acceptance carries a live reading.
  - Please post, against this head (no push), a 10-slice donut in the running Console, in light and in dark. Include either a screenshot of each, or each sector's computed `fill` read with `getComputedStyle`, showing ten resolved, distinct colours.
  - Add one line confirming `--chart-6..10` resolve (are non-empty) on the Console's `:root` and `.dark`.
  - A dashboard widget (the `DashboardRenderer` relay) is the most useful surface for this, since that is where the card saw the repeat.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: Some pairs are close by eye even though each nearest-neighbour distance stays at or above the old floor. In dark, `--chart-4` (280°) sits next to `--chart-7` (300°), and `--chart-5` (340°) next to `--chart-9` (0°). The live screenshots in M1 are where that gets judged. They are not a reason to retune by themselves.

Landing: not governed. After M1 this head is ACCEPT, and area o3-H lands it once CI is fully green on this exact head. A later push owes a delta read.

## Live reading — ten-slice donut, light and dark (2026-11-17T21:14Z)

Answers REWORK M1 (comment 6961009649). This is an evidence-only round: no code was pushed.

**Head:** `856cb45cb1da32a58e4ddc0e4602ceb8d5045c69`, checked out detached in a fresh worktree.

**Surface:** the real Console stylesheet (`ui/apps/console/src/index.css`) under the Console's own Vite config, which aliases `@object-ui/*` to `src`. The widget goes through the real `DashboardRenderer` relay and real Recharts. The widget is `type: 'donut'` with 10 inline rows, `xField: stage`, `yField: total`, and **no authored `colors`**. Rendering is headless Chromium (Playwright `chromium.launch()`, `deviceScaleFactor: 2`). Dark mode is the `dark` class on `html`, the same switch the preview gallery uses.

The harness is two **untracked** files in that worktree, `ui/apps/console/live-34902.html` and `ui/apps/console/src/live-34902.tsx`. They were never committed and are deleted with the worktree. I used this harness instead of the preview gallery because `?only=dashboard` renders the designer, not a data widget with inline rows. The full harness source:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import './index.css';
import { I18nProvider } from '@object-ui/i18n';
import { SchemaRendererProvider } from '@object-ui/react';
import '@object-ui/components';
import '@object-ui/plugin-charts';
import { DashboardRenderer } from '@object-ui/plugin-dashboard';

if (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('theme') === 'dark') {
  document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
}
const rows = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => ({ stage: `Stage ${i + 1}`, total: 10 }));
const widget = {
  id: 'donut10', type: 'donut', title: 'Ten-slice donut (no authored colors)',
  options: { xField: 'stage', yField: 'total' }, data: rows, layout: { x: 0, y: 0, w: 12, h: 6 },
};
const dataSource = { aggregate: async () => [], find: async () => [] };
ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <I18nProvider>
    <SchemaRendererProvider dataSource={dataSource as never}>
      <DashboardRenderer schema={{ widgets: [widget] } as never} />
    </SchemaRendererProvider>
  </I18nProvider>,
);
```

**Commands:**
```
git worktree add --detach ../objectstack-issue-34902-live 856cb45c
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-dashboard^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-charts^...' --filter '@object-ui/i18n...' build"   # VERDICT command-exit 0
cd ui/apps/console && pnpm exec vite --port 52643 --strictPort
node node_modules/.drive-34902.cjs 52643 OUTDIR   # for light and dark: wait for 10 path.recharts-sector, read getComputedStyle(path).fill, screenshot
```

### Console stylesheet: computed sector fills (the binding evidence)

| slice | token | light computed fill | dark computed fill |
|--:|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `--chart-1` | `rgb(36, 99, 235)` | `rgb(60, 131, 246)` |
| 2 | `--chart-2` | `rgb(42, 157, 144)` | `rgb(38, 217, 196)` |
| 3 | `--chart-3` | `rgb(124, 59, 237)` | `rgb(155, 106, 241)` |
| 4 | `--chart-4` | `rgb(251, 146, 60)` | `rgb(251, 157, 80)` |
| 5 | `--chart-5` | `rgb(226, 54, 112)` | `rgb(239, 93, 141)` |
| 6 | `--chart-6` | `rgb(37, 147, 64)` | `rgb(47, 188, 82)` |
| 7 | `--chart-7` | `rgb(147, 26, 117)` | `rgb(190, 55, 156)` |
| 8 | `--chart-8` | `rgb(21, 159, 193)` | `rgb(35, 191, 231)` |

**Light: 10 distinct of 10. Dark: 10 distinct of 10.** Each sector's `fill` attribute is `hsl(var(--chart-N))` with N equal to the slice number. Page errors: 0 in both themes.

The token values resolve non-empty on both `:root` and `.dark`. Read with `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`:
- `:root` `--chart-6..10` = `135 60% 36%, 315 70% 34%, 192 80% 42%, 0 70% 36%, 215 14% 58%`
- `.dark` `--chart-6..10` = `135 60% 46%, 315 55% 48%, 192 80% 52%, 0 70% 48%, 210 12% 68%`

### Library stylesheet (`@object-ui/components`), same widget, for N1

L1's N1 names the library's dark values (chart-4 at 280°, chart-5 at 340°). The Console does not use those values. To judge N1 by eye, I rendered the same widget a second time with `ui/packages/components/src/index.css` in place of the Console stylesheet, using a sibling untracked harness that differs only in that import.

| slice | token | light computed fill | dark computed fill |
|--:|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `--chart-1` | `rgb(231, 110, 80)` | `rgb(38, 98, 217)` |
| 2 | `--chart-2` | `rgb(42, 157, 144)` | `rgb(46, 184, 138)` |
| 3 | `--chart-3` | `rgb(39, 71, 84)` | `rgb(232, 140, 48)` |
| 4 | `--chart-4` | `rgb(232, 196, 104)` | `rgb(175, 87, 219)` |
| 5 | `--chart-5` | `rgb(244, 164, 98)` | `rgb(226, 54, 112)` |
| 6 | `--chart-6` | `rgb(46, 158, 65)` | `rgb(66, 190, 55)` |
| 7 | `--chart-7` | `rgb(160, 34, 128)` | `rgb(223, 144, 223)` |
| 8 | `--chart-8` | `rgb(18, 174, 226)` | `rgb(43, 183, 202)` |
| 9 | `--chart-9` | `rgb(165, 29, 29)` | `rgb(199, 35, 35)` |
| 10 | `--chart-10` | `rgb(124, 138, 156)` | `rgb(141, 153, 165)` |

**Light: 10 distinct of 10. Dark: 10 distinct of 10.** In this variant the legend swatches render without colour. That is a harness artefact: the library sheet does not `@source` the plugin packages, so the legend's Tailwind classes are never generated. The sectors are unaffected.

### N1, judged by eye on the dark screenshots

- **Library dark, chart-4 (280°, `rgb(175, 87, 219)`) vs chart-7 (300°, `rgb(223, 144, 223)`):** I can tell them apart. Chart-4 is a saturated mid purple and chart-7 is a light orchid, and the separation comes mostly from lightness. This is the weakest pair in the palette. A reader with reduced colour vision may struggle with it, and two small legend swatches side by side are harder than two sectors. I would call it acceptable but the closest pair, not comfortable.
- **Library dark, chart-5 (340°, `rgb(226, 54, 112)`) vs chart-9 (0°, `rgb(199, 35, 35)`):** clearly distinct. One is a pink rose and the other a pure, darker red.
- **What the Console actually ships in dark** has no 280° token. Its nearest equivalents are chart-3 violet `rgb(155, 106, 241)` vs chart-7 magenta `rgb(190, 55, 156)`, and chart-5 rose `rgb(239, 93, 141)` vs chart-9 red `rgb(208, 37, 37)`. All four are clearly distinct by eye.

### Screenshots

The relay can only post text, so it cannot upload images. The four PNGs (deviceScaleFactor 2, 1880x1280) are kept in the dev session's scratchpad and handed to the seat with this report. In that directory they are `donut10-light.png` and `donut10-dark.png` (Console stylesheet), and `donut10-lib-light.png` and `donut10-lib-dark.png` (library stylesheet). The rgb tables above are the binding evidence. Any reader can reproduce them with the harness source and commands above.

An observation that is not a finding of this card: the legend lists categories in string order (`Stage 1, Stage 10, Stage 2, ...`). The sectors are in data order. Colours follow the data index, so every swatch still matches its sector.
